description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—for a model, likely an LLM, as it incorporates external feedback. The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from 0.81 to 0.99 on a linear scale, with tick marks at 0.01 intervals. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines every 0.2 units. The blue line with circle markers and vertical error bars represents “Final Accuracy”; it remains relatively stable across the confidence range, hovering between approximately 0.90 and 1.00, with slight dips near 0.86 and 0.95. The green dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars, labeled “Initial Accuracy,” starts at approximately 0.55 at 0.81 confidence, dips to around 0.58 at 0.85, then rises steadily to about 0.95 at 0.99 confidence. The orange dashed line with diamond markers and vertical error bars, labeled “Δ Accuracy” (change in accuracy), begins at approximately 0.45 at 0.81 confidence, declines sharply to near 0.15 at 0.86, fluctuates between 0.15 and 0.35 through the middle range, and drops to nearly 0.0 at 0.99 confidence. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in measurements at each confidence level.
